plan.name: Stop a sandbox's container when its check is cut off
plan.summary: Add toolchain.Docker(ctx, args...) *exec.Cmd in internal/toolchain/docker.go, which returns a command for the docker client. For `run`, it inserts "--name", "invariant-<pid>-<start>-<n>" right after "run" (pid is this process, start its start time, n a counter, so no two containers share a name) and keeps every other argument in order. When the context ends, it runs `docker rm --force <name>` on a fresh, short-lived context and waits for it, whether the container has started or not, then kills the client, with a WaitDelay of a few seconds; a run that finishes by itself is never removed, and every other docker command is left as exec.CommandContext(ctx, "docker", args...). Every `docker run` goes through it: internal/tlc/tlc.go, internal/tlc/graph.go, internal/gobra/gobra.go, internal/verify/existing.go, internal/verify/language.go (two), internal/verify/larger.go (two), internal/verify/nagini.go and internal/plumbing/sandbox.go, and an integration test in internal/verify shows a container sleeping past a three-second deadline returns an error and is gone a few seconds later. This changes the trusted base, so a person merges it.

tests.name: TestDockerRunIsNamedAndKeepsItsArguments
tests.says: A docker run is given --name invariant-<pid>-<start>-<n> right after run, and keeps its other arguments in order.

tests.name: TestDockerLeavesOtherCommandsAsTheyWere
tests.says: Any docker command other than run keeps exactly the arguments it was given.

tests.name: TestDockerNeverGivesTwoContainersOneName
tests.says: Two runs never get the same container name.

tests.name: TestDockerRunRemovesItsContainerWhenItsContextEnds
tests.says: When a run's context ends, its container is removed with docker rm --force <name> and the run returns an error promptly.

tests.name: TestDockerRunLeavesAFinishedContainerAlone
tests.says: A run that finishes on its own is never removed.
